cōmoedia, cōmoediae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a comedy; comedy

The genre and a single play. To put one on is cōmoediam agere (Ter. Heaut. prol.), to watch one spectāre, to read one legere (Plin. Ep. 6.21.2). Pliny called his villa down by the water Cōmoedia and the one on the heights Tragoedia (Plin. Ep. 9.7.3).

Other words

  • cōmicus, cōmica, cōmicum — of comedy, comic; as a noun, a comic poet

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 67: poēta cōmicus (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Capt. 4.1.11: ut cōmicī servī solent (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    What belongs to comedy or appears in it: cōmicī senēs, the stock old men of the stage. It is not “funny” in general (see funny).

  • cōmoedus, cōmoedī m. — comic actor, comedian

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Com. 30; Quint. 1.11.1; Plin. Ep. 1.15.2 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    An actor of comedy, as against histriō, any actor.

Examples

  • cēnantī mihi, sī cum uxōre vel paucīs, liber legitur; post cēnam cōmoedia aut lyristēs

    when I dine with my wife or a few friends, a book is read; after dinner, a comedy or a lyre-playerPlin. Ep. 9.36.4

See also theatre, play, performance, joke, funny.
